clue.text: Thinly sliced beef over butter on one

parts.note: over, as in 'the danger is over', means past
a ram is an animal that butts, so a butter
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A deli order: slices of beef laid over a buttered roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the spread but is read as 'one who butts', the old crossword ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a cured, spiced beef that is served cut into very thin slices.

clue.text: Cartoon character's father on organ

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
the eye is an organ of sight

explanation.surface: A cartoon character's dad is seated at a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second. The 's on the definition is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor is the spinach-eating cartoon hero created by E. C. Segar.

clue.text: Walking in street, waving

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
rolling describes waves moving, as in rolling seas

explanation.surface: Someone walks down the street waving to friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Strolling is walking in a slow, relaxed way, so it is a gentle kind of walking.

clue.text: What a church may have organised for trade unions holding ballot at last

indicators.note: organised means arranged into a new order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of ballot

explanation.surface: A union branch organises a vote, as a church might organise a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Churches often run an appeal to raise money for repairs to an old building, known as a restoration fund.

clue.text: Painter, male, in dispute (not with university)

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

indicators.note: not with means without, so the abbreviation that follows is taken out

parts.note: a matter in dispute is at issue
U is the abbreviation for university; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A male painter is caught up in an argument that has nothing to do with his university.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French artist who led the Fauvist movement and made famous paper cut-outs.

clue.text: Duck emerging from bird shelter in outskirts of Stranraer

indicators.note: in places the shelter inside the edge letters of the town name
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the Scottish town
a cote is a small house for doves or other birds

explanation.surface: A duck waddles out of a dovecote on the edge of a Scottish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stranraer is a port town in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck found off northern coasts, so a particular kind of the bird.

clue.text: Take mercer north, possibly to create a monopoly

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements the letters could take

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cloth dealer is moved up north to build a business empire.
explanation.walkthrough: A mercer is a dealer in fine fabrics.
explanation.definitionFit: To corner the market is to gain control of the supply of a commodity, which amounts to having a monopoly.

clue.text: Coronet found in Tahiti, a rarity

indicators.note: found in says the word sits inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the island name, the article and the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A rare jewelled crown turns up on a Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, much like a small crown or coronet.

clue.text: Poet is, to sister, remarkable

indicators.note: remarkable means out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of their ordinary order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet is a remarkable figure in the eyes of her sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting surface: Christina Rossetti was the sister of the painter-poet Dante Gabriel Rossetti.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina and Dante Gabriel Rossetti were both Victorian poets, so either answers to the name.

clue.text: Get back about company in the capital

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Co is the abbreviation for company
going to London is going up to town, so being in the capital is being up

explanation.surface: A firm moves back into town after time away from London.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go 'up' to London from anywhere else, so being in the capital is being up.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup a loss is to get back the money spent, so the verb means regain.

clue.text: He abducted Helen in capital

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Trojan prince who carried off Helen of Sparta
second meaning: the capital city of France

explanation.surface: A kidnapper is tracked down hiding in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Trojan prince of this name took Helen, starting the Trojan War; the same name belongs to the French capital.

clue.text: Means of deciding winners from couples describing holiday

indicators.note: describing is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line around something

parts.note: to couple things is to tie them, so couples are ties
a short holiday is a break

explanation.surface: Couples talk about their holiday as if it settled some competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is the geometric sense, drawing around, so one word wraps the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, tiebreaks are extra games played to settle a set that is level, so they decide who wins.

clue.text: Body of water comprised of three colours

parts.note: first colour: the hue of a lemon
second colour: a pale greyish beige
third colour: lake is a deep red pigment, as in crimson lake

explanation.surface: A painter describes a pond as nothing more than three shades.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake is a pigment name, a purplish red, which few solvers think of as a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowstone Lake is the largest high-altitude lake in North America, inside Yellowstone National Park.

clue.text: Copyright infringer could make head of paper extremely angry

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of paper
irate means very angry

explanation.surface: Someone stealing material from a newspaper would make its editor furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is someone who copies and sells work without the copyright holder's permission.

clue.text: Uncomplaining convalescent

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bearing delay or trouble calmly
second meaning: a person recovering under medical care

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of a good hospital case, but the adjective and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for calm endurance and also a noun for someone receiving medical treatment.

clue.text: Spain lost, meeting Italy at home in match, so put out

indicators.note: in places the at-home word inside the word for a match

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
L stands for lost in league tables
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
a match is a mate, a partner or companion
being at home is being in

explanation.surface: A football report: Spain lose a home match against Italy and are knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'lost' and 'match' look like sports talk; they are an abbreviation and a word for a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate a team is to put it out of a competition.

clue.text: Get on with Oscar, Miranda's father

parts.note: to get on in life is to prosper
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Advice to get along with a man named Oscar, who is the father of Miranda.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's The Tempest, the magician Prospero is the father of Miranda.

clue.text: Anger shown about boy's Scott Joplin music

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for anger goes round the boy

parts.note: rage is fierce anger
a boy's name; the 's joins the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross about a lad's taste in old piano tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott Joplin was the leading composer of ragtime, the syncopated piano style of around 1900.

clue.text: Social occasions, still extremely tedious

parts.note: still and even both intensify a comparison, as in 'still better' or 'even better'

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the following word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of tedious

explanation.surface: Someone complains that parties remain deeply boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Events are organised happenings such as parties, galas or receptions, which are social occasions.

clue.text: Fielding heroine, one trapped by a sly male

indicators.note: trapped by puts the numeral inside the other letters
something sly is devious and twisted, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A novel's heroine falls into the clutches of a cunning man.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Fielding wrote the novel Amelia (1751); 'Fielding' is the author, not cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia Booth is the virtuous title heroine of Henry Fielding's last novel.

clue.text: Serious opera lacking capital before

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its initial letter, and lacking it means that letter goes

parts.note: Faust is the opera by Gounod
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A grave opera that has lost its funding, as it was before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but means the first letter of the opera's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern and severe in manner, which is a sense of serious.

clue.text: Customer in court defending right

indicators.note: defending means guarding by standing all around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Ct is the abbreviation for court
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A lawyer's customer is in court, where the right is being defended.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal surface hides that the lawyer's word 'right' is the technical term for a claim on property.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is someone who buys services from a professional, so a customer of a lawyer or business.

clue.text: Dog in well? Boy put in well, then left

parts.note: a spring is a natural well of water

indicators.note: put in means one word is placed inside another, here the boy wrapping the resort

parts.note: a boy's name
a spa is a mineral spring or well
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A dog has fallen down a well, and a boy goes down after it.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrasing is loose: the second well sits inside the boy's name rather than the boy inside the well.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer spaniel is a breed of gun dog used to flush game.

clue.text: Breed fish, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: rays are flat fish

explanation.surface: Instructions to farm fish, or so it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise animals is to breed and rear them, as in raising cattle.

clue.text: Form quite unpredictable — better discounting both sides

indicators.note: unpredictable letters do not keep a fixed order, so they are rearranged
discounting both sides means leaving off the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its ends are removed

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's form guide is too erratic to bet on, so ignore it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form', meaning proper conduct, sounds like racing form beside 'better' (one who bets).
explanation.definitionFit: Good form is correct social behaviour, which is what etiquette prescribes.

clue.text: Card (king) Welshman put back

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in cards and chess

indicators.note: put back means turned round to face the other way, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh card player puts a king back into the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is the old name for the jack, the playing card below the queen.

clue.text: Exaggerate concerning reception

parts.note: over means about, as in 'a row over money'
a do is a party or social reception

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are overplaying it about a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to carry it too far, which is what exaggerating a gesture or story means.

clue.text: Robe with slit worn by saint — me?

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone surrounds them, so the opening wraps around the words that follow

parts.note: a vent is a slit in the back or side of a coat
St is the abbreviation for saint
taken as written

explanation.surface: A saint wonders whether a slit robe is really for him.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial robe worn by clergy when conducting services.
